title: Automatic program verification
question: Build a program verifier that infers missing assertions and uses them to prove the supplied program correct.
status_note: Automatic assertion discovery and verification have substantial implementations, including property-directed invariant generation. The exercise does not specify a single completeness or performance criterion, so it is not a binary solved/open conjecture.
sources: [{"title": "Bradley and Manna, Property-Directed Incremental Invariant Generation", "url": "https://theory.stanford.edu/~arbrad/papers/pdiig.pdf", "year": null}, {"title": "Software Verification with PDR: Implementation and Empirical Evaluation", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06271", "year": 2019}]

title: Replicative functional equations
question: Classify functions satisfying Knuth's replication identities, including continuous solutions and the more general identities with scale-dependent coefficients.
status_note: Regularity-restricted classifications were already known to the book: its answer gives the continuous case and cites Yoder (1975). Lucht develops related systems of functional equations. This is not a claim to classify all unrestricted functions in every generalized identity.
sources: [{"title": "Lucht, Arithmetical sequences and systems of functional equations", "url": "https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN356261603_0053/PPN356261603_0053.pdf", "year": 1997}]

title: Average cost of saddle-point searches
question: Compare the three proposed matrix saddle-point search algorithms under both random distinct entries and random binary entries.
status_note: Hofri and Jacquet analyze Knuth's three saddle-point search algorithms. The official amendment lowers the exercise to HM42; detailed machine-instruction accounting still depends on the chosen implementation.
sources: [{"title": "Hofri and Jacquet, Saddle Points in Random Matrices: Analysis of Knuth Search Algorithms", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1007/PL00009237", "year": 1998}]
official_updates: [{"date": "1997-04-24", "rating": "HM42", "note": "Rating lowered after average-case analysis.", "url": "https://www-cs-faculty.stanford.edu/~knuth/all1-prepre.ps.gz"}]

title: Counting deque permutations
question: Count the permutations obtainable using a deque, a queue that permits insertion and removal at either end.
status_note: Elvey Price and Guttmann give exact enumeration through functional equations. This settles enumeration in that sense; it is not a closed elementary formula or a rigorous full asymptotic expansion.
sources: [{"title": "Elvey Price and Guttmann, Permutations sortable by deques and by two stacks in parallel", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02273", "year": 2015}, {"title": "Elvey Price, Permutations sortable by deques and two stacks in parallel share the same growth rate", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.00056", "year": 2019}]

title: Linear extensions of the Boolean lattice
question: Count the orders of all subsets of an n-element set that respect inclusion; the amended exercise requests a sharp asymptotic estimate.
status_note: Brightwell and Tetali determine the leading logarithmic asymptotics for the number of linear extensions. That does not give an asymptotic equivalent with ratio tending to one, as requested by the amended sharp-asymptotic question.
sources: [{"title": "Brightwell and Tetali, The Number of Linear Extensions of the Boolean Lattice", "url": "https://doi.org/10.1023/B:ORDE.0000034596.50352.f7", "year": 2003}]
official_updates: [{"date": "2018-03-15", "rating": "HM48", "note": "The request is sharpened to a sharp asymptotic estimate.", "url": "https://www-cs-faculty.stanford.edu/~knuth/all1-pre.ps.gz"}]

title: Topological sorting on tapes
question: Design the most efficient topological sorting algorithm when the graph exceeds internal memory and all external storage is sequential magnetic tape.
status_note: External-memory topological-sorting algorithms were located, but block I/O and semi-external algorithms do not establish optimality in this exercise's sequential-tape model. No resolution of that exact optimization question was located.

title: Average behavior of the buddy allocator

status_note: Stochastic models and partial buddy-system analyses exist, including Purdom–Stigler as discussed in the book. No general average analysis matching both of the specified algorithms and a fully specified request model was located. The answer depends on that model.

title: Infinitely many Mersenne primes

title: Janson's chain-CSP probability asymptotics
question: In the random chain dependency graph, every vertex i > m independently chooses two distinct earlier predecessors. Let c_(m,n) be the probability that every vertex is reachable from vertex n by following predecessor edges. For fixed m, is c_(m,n) = (rho + o(1))^n with a constant rho < 1?
status_note: Janson establishes the asymptotic number of descendants and moment results. The exponential-rate conjecture concerns the much rarer event that all vertices are descendants; no proof of that assertion was verified.

title: Optimal search trees with two-way comparisons
